title: Learning from a Check
summary: Work through Learning from a Check.

blocks.md: This lesson covers the book's section on **Learning from a Check**. Read the excerpt, then test yourself below.

blocks.source: Vol III, Reinforcement Learning from Verifiable Rewards, § Learning from a Check
blocks.md: The previous chapter left the repair agent (a later section) with `trained_policy_v1`, a supervised checkpoint fitted to the one malformed-argument recovery that curation admitted. Its release gate already had to send trials into a state the corpus never covered, the version conflict for which no demonstration exists (a later section). More imitation needs someone to record that recovery, and a preference pair needs two admissible records of it. The agent's versioned test fixtures and acceptance checks need neither.

blocks.prompt: Think first: In two or three sentences, explain why Credit assignment matters for the system this section describes.
blocks.md: Compare your answer with the book's claim: A terminal reward gives every turn the same reward-to-go, so separating a useful step from a faulty one is bought with a critic, more samples, or step-level signals, each at its own cost.

questions.q: The section **Learning from a Check** develops one of the chapter's claims. Which one?
options: Ratios and gradients are valid only on per-invocation records of the delivered prefix token IDs, sampled token IDs, and behavior log probabilities under the actual sampling transforms.
The false-accept share of rewarded rollouts moves with the policy's current pass rate rather than being a fixed verifier property, so reward shaping must preserve the priority of correct outcomes.
RLVR scores sampled rollouts with a programmatic check, so the update learns only what the sampler reaches and the reward distinguishes, and a task the policy never solves gives zero signal.
A terminal reward gives every turn the same reward-to-go, so separating a useful step from a faulty one is bought with a critic, more samples, or step-level signals, each at its own cost.
